vulnerability_mechanism.evidence: In affected code, getMatchedAction() gives req.originalUrl, including its query string, to Cedar action matchers, while Express dispatches using the path. Thus /users/?x=1 can match the less restrictive /users/{id} Cedar action but execute the restrictive /users route. The direct-fix regression tests permit /users/123 and deny /users, /users/?x=1, and the multiple-query variant. CVE.org remains PUBLISHED and the GHSA is not withdrawn.

atomic_bic.evidence: git log -S 'req.originalUrl' and separate git log -L traces for both assignments identify a8cd22f862f6e4a80d187f24062219e02271a3d1 as their first write when src/index.ts was created. It is a single-parent, non-merge source commit, package version 0.1.0, rather than a move, refactor, revert, tag-only release, or later aggregate.

immediate_parent_absence.evidence: The sole immediate parent is df70ec08c60ad0a8c7c4dbb182424b72ea6b2679. That tree has no src/index.ts and git grep finds no originalUrl occurrence; the parent-to-BIC range contains exactly one commit.

squash_member_decomposition.evidence: a8cd22f862f6e4a80d187f24062219e02271a3d1 has one parent, no associated GitHub pull request, and no reconstructable finer public member. It is therefore the smallest surviving public first-write; no squash decomposition is applicable.

affected_release_membership.evidence: The BIC is the 0.1.0 source commit and is an ancestor of tags v0.1.1, v0.1.2, and last-affected v0.2.0. Each inspected affected tag retains both req.originalUrl assignments. GitHub lists <=0.2.0 affected; CVE.org lists versions <0.3.0 affected.

fixed_release_membership.evidence: Fix 3d23c4a23d5537f605d242f6095b22c488df74b8 is not an ancestor of v0.2.0 but is an ancestor of v0.3.0 (tag commit ef73cd0117553e39f7caac27a39c7b8e3d737797). The v0.3.0 tree uses req.path at both formerly vulnerable assignments, matching the GHSA first-patched version 0.3.0.

direct_fix_or_unpatched_state.evidence: 3d23c4a23d5537f605d242f6095b22c488df74b8 directly replaces both req.originalUrl assignments with req.path and adds focused action-matching regression tests. Its immediate parent is v0.2.0 commit eb8fc4300738bd3117e6f125303a54e532091340, which still contains the vulnerable code.

bic_only_ai_attribution.evidence: The BIC commit object names Victor Moreno <morevct@amazon.com> as both author and committer and contains only the message 'v 0.1' plus a matching Signed-off-by trailer. Exact local and GitHub commit metadata show no Co-Authored-By, Generated-with, AI-tool, bot, web-flow, or associated-PR signal. Later commits and the fix were not used to attribute the BIC.

findings: The primary record correctly identifies the authorization bypass: Cedar selected an action from the query-bearing originalUrl while Express executed the query-free path.
The primary record correctly identifies a8cd22f862f6e4a80d187f24062219e02271a3d1 as the atomic BIC and df70ec08c60ad0a8c7c4dbb182424b72ea6b2679 as its verified clean immediate parent.
The affected-through-v0.2.0 and fixed-in-v0.3.0 release gates, including direct fix 3d23c4a23d5537f605d242f6095b22c488df74b8, independently reproduce.
BIC-only attribution independently supports NOT_AI: the surviving commit metadata are human-authored and contain no AI-generation marker.
